$comment: Vendored dependency manifest (ADR 0021). tools/repo/vendor.luau imports each dependency at the pinned commit and re-applies patches/. Rows below carry the TARGET versions from docs/research/ecosystem-2026.md; the 'commit' fields are filled with real SHAs at vendor time (milestone M0) and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is regenerated in the same commit. Adding/upgrading a dependency requires a human-approved ADR (rule R5).
$comment_binaries: ADR 0032 amends ADR 0021 with a second row kind. A row with "kind": "binary" is NOT a source tree: it is a build-time release artifact, fetched at configure time into a cache under $LUAUG_BUILD_ROOT and pinned by SHA256 per platform, never committed. The hash IS the pin -- a mismatch is a hard configure error, and changing one is a human edit here, exactly as changing a commit SHA is. This exists for artifacts whose source form is disproportionate to their role (DXC's source is a fork of LLVM); anything the engine links is still vendored as source.
$comment_toolchains: ADR 0091 adds a third row kind. A row under "toolchains" is a tool built FROM SOURCE by tools/repo/toolchain.luau, outside the repository (under $LUAUG_BUILD_ROOT), at a pinned commit whose submodules are pinned too -- git's own hashes are the pin, and the tool refuses a checkout that does not match every one. It is never vendored and never committed. Unlike a binary row it IS redistributed: `redistributed` says so, and the editor package carries its build and its licence texts.

binaries.name: dxc
binaries.note: The HLSL front-end SDL_shadercross needs (ADR 0006), for the ENGINE's own shaders at the engine's own build. Never redistributed: the editor ships the source-built compiler in the toolchains row below instead (ADR 0091). Not vendored and not committed: see ADR 0032 -- the archives carry an unassigned Microsoft EULA alongside the NCSA licence their own ReleaseNotes.md names, and 50 MiB of opaque binaries would land in history per version. Hashes below are the ones SDL_shadercross itself pins, verified byte-for-byte against the published release. No macOS artifact exists; Microsoft publishes none.

toolchains.name: dxc
toolchains.note: The compiler the EDITOR ships so a user's surface shader compiles on the user's machine (ADR 0091). Built from source, which carries no Microsoft terms -- only the NCSA licence and the notices ThirdPartyNotices.txt lists -- and emits hashed DXIL that retail D3D12 accepts with no dxil.dll (U-64, confirmed 2026-09-25). Measured: 5 min 23 s on Windows x64 at -j14, 295 s on Linux x64 in the Tier-2 image; dxcompiler is 21 MB on Windows and 37.5 MB on Linux. Built once per version and platform by `lute tools/repo/toolchain.luau build dxc`, and by CI's dxc-source job, which caches it by commit.

dependencies.name: luau
dependencies.note: The one patch routes the `^` operator and its constant folding through `luaug_dpow`, the engine's own pow (ADR 0083), because the C runtime's pow rounds differently on each platform and a script's `x ^ y` is on the simulation's path. The engine defines the symbol and links it into Luau.VM and Luau.Compiler.

dependencies.name: sdl3
dependencies.note: Two local patches. 0001 (D182): the D3D12 backend wrote GPU descriptor groups past the end of its descriptor heaps and replaced heaps mid-bind; still present upstream on 2026-09-24. The patch reserves room for a whole draw or dispatch before writing and rebinds every table after a heap replacement. 0002 (ADR 0091): on a lost device, pushing uniform data dereferenced the NULL uniform buffer the pool returned, so a GPU reset crashed the process inside SDL; the patch drops the data instead. To be sent upstream; drop each when a pinned release carries its fix.

dependencies.name: sdl_shadercross
dependencies.note: Has never cut a release: no tags exist at all, so the version is the pinned commit's date (same treatment as stb).

dependencies.name: spirv_cross
dependencies.note: Pinned at the revision SDL_shadercross's own submodule points to, which is what upstream CI tests against. Required unconditionally by its CMakeLists.txt:145-158; there is no build without it.

dependencies.name: jolt
dependencies.note: Vendored at M5, the milestone that first needs it -- the row and its version have existed since planning (ADR 0007) and the roadmap permits vendoring lazily provided the row does, which is the xxhash and meshoptimizer rule. The commit is the v5.6.0 tag, read off upstream with `vendor.luau resolve` rather than recalled.

dependencies.name: box2d
dependencies.note: Vendored at post-v1 phase 3, the phase that first needs it (ADR 0008 committed the version at planning; the owner opened the phase on 2026-09-23). The commit is the v3.1.1 tag, read off upstream with `vendor.luau resolve` rather than recalled. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: the library is `include/` and `src/`; the samples application, its fonts and its bundled GLFW/imgui/glad, the benchmark data and the unit-test runner are an application we do not build. Compiled by `third_party/CMakeLists.txt` from its sources directly, not through upstream CMake, which configures the samples by default.

dependencies.name: miniaudio
dependencies.note: Vendored at M6, the milestone that first needs it -- the row and its version have existed since planning (ADR 0009) and the roadmap permits vendoring lazily provided the row does, which is the xxhash, meshoptimizer and Jolt rule. The commit is the 0.11.25 tag, read off upstream with `vendor.luau resolve` rather than recalled. Only miniaudio.h and miniaudio.c are compiled; the extras/ and research/ trees are carried for reference.

dependencies.name: fastgltf
dependencies.note: Requires simdjson unconditionally (CMakeLists.txt:77-82) and downloads it unpinned into deps/ when no simdjson::simdjson target exists. We define that target first and the patch turns the download branch into a FATAL_ERROR -- ADR 0036.

dependencies.name: simdjson
dependencies.note: fastgltf's mandatory dependency (ADR 0036), pinned at the version its own CMake targets -- the same rule the spirv_cross row follows. Only singleheader/simdjson.{h,cpp} is compiled; the pair is committed upstream and is exactly what fastgltf would otherwise fetch.

dependencies.name: basis_universal
dependencies.note: Vendored at M7, the milestone that first needs a texture pipeline (ADR 0010). Two targets rather than one: the TRANSCODER (transcoder/basisu_transcoder.cpp) is linked into the runtime, and the ENCODER (encoder/*.cpp) only into the offline `assetc` tool -- the engine must never be able to write a texture. Encoder settings are pinned to standardized UASTC/ETC1S; docs/research/ecosystem-2026.md:193 records that XUASTC was still not standardized in early 2026, and a non-portable texture format is the last thing an asset pipeline should reach for. The KTX-Software row beside this one stays unpinned: basis writes and reads the KTX2 container itself, so the pairing partner would be a large tree with its own dependency set bought for a format both halves of which are already here. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: upstream's tree at this commit is 302 MB, of which 275 MB is test images, prebuilt binaries, WebGL demos and Python wheels that nothing here compiles -- and 49 MB of it is exactly the opaque binaries ADR 0032 exists to keep out of history. The nine paths listed are checked out by git pathspec, so what lands is still byte-exact upstream at the pinned commit; what is given up is the whole-tree rule.

dependencies.name: stb
dependencies.note: stb has no tags; version is the pinned commit's date. tests/oversample/oversample.exe is a prebuilt binary upstream's own .gitignore ignores, so it is untracked there and never checked out here -- the tree is byte-exact upstream, and that file's absence is upstream's decision rather than a deviation of ours.

dependencies.name: imgui
dependencies.note: The docking branch, per ADR 0011. Byte-exact upstream, which this note previously claimed it was not: it described excluding examples/libs/glfw/lib-vc2010-{32,64}/glfw3.lib, and those files have been tracked here since M0. The tree is upstream's tracked files by construction (ADR 0021) and the note is now what the repository actually contains. examples/example_android_opengl3/android/gradle/ is absent because upstream's own nested .gitignore leaves it untracked, not because we exclude it. Only core/ and backends/{sdl3,sdlgpu3} are compiled; the examples/ tree is carried for reference only.

dependencies.name: recastnavigation
dependencies.note: Vendored at M7 with the seam only (ADR 0022) and **integrated in post-v1 phase 3 by ADR 0089**: `engine/nav` builds a tiled navmesh with Recast and answers from it with Detour, and `third_party/CMakeLists.txt` compiles Recast, Detour and -- since ADR 0098's crowds -- DetourCrowd (DetourTileCache stays on disk, unbuilt, until something calls it). **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: RecastDemo alone carries SDL, bundled fonts and sample meshes for an application we do not build, and `Tests` pulls Catch2 -- a second test framework in a repository that pins doctest (R5). The four library directories are the library.

dependencies.name: gamenetworkingsockets
dependencies.note: DELIBERATELY NOT VENDORED AT M7, and this note is the reason rather than the absence of one (human decision, 2026-08-21). ADR 0012 names GNS as the default transport behind `ITransport` and ENet as the alternative; v1 ships primitives only, and M7 scope is a loopback echo example -- replication is post-v1. GNS depends on OpenSSL-or-libsodium PLUS protobuf (docs/research/ecosystem-2026.md:210), none of which has a row here: protobuf is a code generator that invades the build and OpenSSL is a compilation problem on all four tiers, bought for a seam with no v1 caller. What v1 needs is the SEAM, not the implementation behind it, so `ITransport` is frozen with ENet as its one implementation and this row waits -- the same shape ADR 0040 used for Clay, and the same lazy-vendoring rule the Jolt row followed until M5. Whoever builds replication post-v1 finds the reasoning here instead of re-deriving it.

dependencies.name: enet
dependencies.note: Vendored at M7 as the ONE implementation behind `ITransport` (ADR 0012). The row beside it -- gamenetworkingsockets -- explains why it is the only one: v1 ships primitives and a loopback echo, replication is post-v1, and ENet is a single C library with no dependencies at all, which is the whole reason ADR 0012 names it as the alternative rather than as a second default. UDP with optional reliability and sequencing, and nothing else: no encryption, no authentication. That is stated here because it is a property a caller must know rather than a gap to be filled later -- an ENet channel is a LAN or a trusted link, and anything else waits for the GNS row to be filled in.

dependencies.name: assimp
dependencies.note: Offline importer tool ONLY -- never linked into the runtime (ADR 0010). It is a dependency of `assetc`, and the layering gate plus this note are what keep it there: the engine reads `.lmesh`, a format assimp has never heard of. glTF stays on fastgltf even though assimp can read it, because the runtime pipeline's importer and the exotic-format importer are different jobs and fastgltf is the one M4 proved. Configured with a NARROW importer set and every exporter off (third_party/CMakeLists.txt): assimp's default build is about sixty importers, most of them formats nobody has shipped this decade, and each one is compile time plus attack surface on a tool that reads untrusted files. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: upstream's tree is dominated by `test/models`, hundreds of megabytes of sample assets in the exotic formats themselves -- the very binaries ADR 0032 exists to keep out of history, and useless to us because we do not run assimp's own test suite.

dependencies.name: blake3
dependencies.note: Vendored at M7, the milestone that first needs a ContentHash -- the row and its licence have existed since planning (architecture.md section 2) and the roadmap permits vendoring lazily provided the row does, which is the xxhash, meshoptimizer, Jolt and miniaudio rule. Only c/blake3.c, c/blake3_dispatch.c and c/blake3_portable.c are compiled, with BLAKE3_NO_{SSE2,SSE41,AVX2,AVX512} defined: the SIMD paths need per-file compiler flags or assembler, and a content ADDRESS that depended on which instruction set the build machine had would be a cache key that is not a name. The Rust crate and the reference implementation are carried for reference.

dependencies.name: xxhash
dependencies.note: WorldHash is specified as xxh3 (architecture.md §9). Vendored at M2, which is the milestone that first needs it -- the manifest row has existed since planning and M0's scope permits vendoring lazily provided the row does.

dependencies.name: inter
dependencies.note: The engine's DEFAULT TYPEFACE (human decision, 2026-08-20; roadmap M7). One face, not several: a good default plus "bring your own" covers the ground, and three vendored faces are three things to licence, update and explain. Roboto (Apache-2.0) was the alternative if matching this repository's own licence family were worth more than the typeface, and it is not. OFL 1.1 is a permissive licence for R6's purposes -- it allows redistribution and embedding, and its one real condition is that the font not be sold on its own, which nothing here does. It also forbids using the RESERVED FONT NAME on a modified copy; this vendors the file unmodified, which is ADR 0021's rule anyway. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: upstream is a type-design repository -- sources, build tooling, a web specimen site and every previously released binary. What a game engine needs from it is one file and the licence. `InterVariable.ttf` rather than a static instance because upstream ships no static TTF at this tag; stb_truetype reads its default instance, and `engine/ui`'s atlas test asserts the rendered weight is Regular rather than trusting that.
